text: Why must the grammar be written with `*` rather than as `expression := expression '+' term`?
choices: The second requires two tokens of lookahead, which recursive descent cannot supply.
The second would build a right-associative tree, which is wrong for subtraction.
The second is left-recursive, so the generated method calls itself having consumed nothing — immediate stack overflow.
The second is ambiguous, since it permits both left and right groupings.
explanation: `expression()` would begin by calling `expression()` at the same position and recurse forever. Rewriting left recursion as iteration is the standard transformation, and it is why the parser has `while` loops where the grammar has stars. It is one of the two real limits of the technique; the other is that the grammar must be decidable with limited lookahead.
